clue.text: Male to go on a diet avoiding certain foods

parts.note: dieting means you eat less, so the phrase gives EAT LESS

explanation.surface: A man resolves to start dieting by cutting out certain foods.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetarian diet shuns flesh, so a menu without it avoids one particular class of foods.

clue.text: Ordinary couple crossing European river

indicators.note: crossing says the couple word spans the river, which sits inside it

parts.note: to couple animals is to mate them
the Oder flows between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A typical pair make their way across a river on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate means middling or average, a synonym for ordinary in the sense of unremarkable.

clue.text: Struggle to get in commercial payment?

indicators.note: to get in says the struggle word enters the commercial word

parts.note: a commercial on TV is an ad
a war is a struggle

explanation.surface: A fight to get into advertising pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a prize or damages is only loosely a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's award of damages is a sum paid out, so it is a kind of payment.

clue.text: Kit offers joke going down in toboggan

indicators.note: going down in says the joke word descends into the toboggan word in this down clue

parts.note: a luge is a small racing toboggan
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Gear offers a laugh as it slides about in a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit in the sense of one's belongings packed for travel is baggage.

clue.text: Faction posturing

definitions.meaning: a group or team in a dispute
pretentious airs, as in putting on airs and graces

explanation.surface: A political group is accused of mere posturing.
explanation.definitionFit: One takes a team in a contest; British slang also uses the word for haughty swagger or pretension.

clue.text: Endless trumpets etc with incoming of Queen's composer

indicators.note: incoming means the Queen's letters come into the shortened instrument word
endless says the final letter of the brass section word is cut off

parts.note: trumpets and their kin make up the brass of an orchestra
HM stands for Her Majesty, the Queen

explanation.surface: An orchestra's trumpets announce the arrival of the Queen's favourite composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the final letter of the trumpets word, leaving BRAS; 'with incoming of' sets the royal letters inside it, before its last letter. 'Queen's' looks possessive but gives Her Majesty's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Brahms is a celebrated German Romantic composer, so he is an example of the class named.

clue.text: Havin' an inclination to hug this person, being a dish

indicators.note: to hug says the setter word is held inside the sloping word

parts.note: raking means sloping, so having an incline, here clipped to rakin'
the setter speaking of himself is me

explanation.surface: Someone with an urge to embrace the speaker, being a real looker.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g of 'Havin'' signals that the sloping word is clipped to RAKIN as well. 'Dish' also suggests an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small ovenproof bowl for baking individual portions.

clue.text: Greeting given to small knight when masquerade occurs

parts.note: hallo is a variant of hello
wee is Scottish for small
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A little knight is greeted when a costume ball takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: On All Hallows' Eve people dress up in costumes, so the night is a time of disguise.

clue.text: Spring ceremony for a fairy

parts.note: SP is a dictionary abbreviation for spring, as in a water source
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A seasonal ritual held in honour of a woodland fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or small magical being, a kind of fairy in folklore.

clue.text: Inappropriately mentioned being teased in a provincial party

indicators.note: in says the teasing word sits inside the party initials

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, often called the Province
to rag someone is to tease them, so being teased is ragged

explanation.surface: Someone is mocked at a regional political gathering for raising an awkward subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is known in Britain as 'the Province', so a provincial party is the DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag up an old matter is an idiom for raising it when it would be better left alone.

clue.text: Time Lord's going around facing attack? Who transcends time

indicators.note: going around says the lord word surrounds the time letter

parts.note: a lord is a peer, and the 's is short for is
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A Time Lord circles before an assault: who is beyond time itself?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time Lord' suggests Doctor Who, but the words split: Time gives T and Lord gives PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: J M Barrie's boy who never grows up stays forever young, untouched by the passing years.

clue.text: Containing a certain amount of substance used for grinding

definitions.text: Containing a certain amount of substance
definitions.meaning: in chemistry, describing a solution by its moles of substance per litre
a back tooth that chews and grinds food

explanation.surface: Something holding a measured quantity of material is employed for milling.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists call concentration in moles per litre this; dentists use it for the broad back teeth that grind.

clue.text: Tire in America, being left-wing, not Conservative

indicators.note: not says the Conservative letter is taken away from the left-wing word

parts.note: radical describes someone of the far left

explanation.surface: An American grows weary of being left-wing rather than a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tire' looks like a verb meaning weary, but it is the American spelling of tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial is a type of tyre with cords running across it, which Americans spell tire.

clue.text: Keep an eye on punter's money on the table?

parts.note: a punter (a gambler) puts down a stake
cards or cash laid on the table are out, in plain view

explanation.surface: A gambler is told to watch the cash laid on the betting table.
explanation.definitionFit: Police on a stakeout watch a place covertly, so to do this is to keep surveillance on it.

clue.text: Rodent invading an avens or some other plant

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: invading says the rodent word enters the avens phrase

parts.note: geum is the botanical genus of avens
a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A rat burrows into a flowering avens or some other garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageratum, or floss flower, is a garden bedding plant with fluffy blue blooms.

clue.text: Arrange tent on ground somewhere in France

indicators.note: ground means crushed or worked over, so the preceding words' letters are milled into a new order

explanation.surface: Campers are told to pitch their tent on level ground at a French site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'ground' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarn-et-Garonne is a department in southern France, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Fixing break with rubber seal

parts.note: a rest is a break
an O-ring is a rubber gasket

explanation.surface: Mending a crack with a rubber seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Restoring old furniture means repairing it, so the word is a synonym for mending.

clue.text: Writer whose output once shed some light

definitions.text: whose output once shed some light
definitions.meaning: a maker of candles, the old light source

explanation.surface: An author whose work once illuminated something.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote hard-boiled detective fiction; a candle maker's products historically gave light.

clue.text: The soldier, man in conflict for an astronomical time

indicators.note: in conflict suggests the letters of the soldier phrase are thrown into turmoil and reordered

explanation.surface: A soldier spends an astronomically long time fighting in a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidereal month is the moon's orbital period measured against the stars, a unit of astronomy.

clue.text: Take away pamphlet after upsetting editor

indicators.note: after says the pamphlet word comes after the editor letters
upsetting in a down clue means the editor letters are turned upside down

parts.note: a tract is a pamphlet

explanation.surface: A pamphlet is withdrawn after the editor is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to diminish it, taking away from its worth.

clue.text: Fuss about animal noises? Quite the opposite in country areas

indicators.note: about would put the fuss word around the noises word
quite the opposite reverses the roles, so the noises word goes around the fuss word

parts.note: mews are the cries of cats
ado is fuss

explanation.surface: Someone frets over farmyard sounds, or perhaps the reverse, out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'about' would put the fuss word round the noises; 'Quite the opposite' flips which piece contains which.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadows are grassy fields, typical of rural landscapes.

clue.text: Go for each flavour

parts.note: go means energy, vigour, as does pep
per means for each

explanation.surface: Choose one seasoning for every dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper food is to season it, so the verb means to flavour.

clue.text: Without ribs in a country that's totally green?

definitions.meaning: a botanical term for leaves lacking ribs or costae
read as eco plus state, a nation wholly devoted to environmentalism

explanation.surface: An environmentally pure nation is imagined as having no ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use the term for structures lacking costae, while a fully ecological nation would be an eco state.

clue.text: French native dances, switching sides

indicators.note: switching sides says the two halves of the dance word swap places

parts.note: congas are Latin American line dances

explanation.surface: A Frenchman dances, changing partners from one side to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gascon is someone from Gascony, a region of south-west France.

clue.text: Island decided to discharge prisoner

indicators.note: to discharge says the convict is released, removed from the word

parts.note: concrete means definite, decided
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: An island's authorities resolve to release an inmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Drive in which one's well up, having lost the lead

indicators.note: having lost the lead says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to surge is to well up

explanation.surface: A car journey where one feels emotional after losing the dog's leash.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is an impulse or drive, a powerful inner push.

clue.text: Sherpa is abject — minimal money pocketed

indicators.note: pocketed says the letters are tucked away inside the words Sherpa is abject

explanation.surface: A mountain guide is wretched after being handed a tiny tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The paisa is a hundredth of a rupee, a very small coin in South Asian currencies.

clue.text: Spoil dinner? Nothing right in it, like marble!

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: in it says the nothing-and-right letters go inside the dinner word

parts.note: dinner is a meal
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A ruined dinner leaves the diners as cold and stony as marble.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmoreal is a literary adjective meaning made of or resembling marble, cold and white.

clue.text: True love is OK!

parts.note: true can mean right, correct
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Being in genuine love is declared to be fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-o is a breezy British interjection of agreement, much like saying fine or sure.

clue.text: A comment about the troopers? No big girl's blouses!

definitions.meaning: read as ..., a remark on how soldiers talk
clothing for men, so nothing feminine; a big girl's blouse is British slang for a weak man

explanation.surface: An outburst about soldiers: no wimps allowed among them!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big girl's blouse' is British slang for a feeble, unmanly man; here it is also taken literally as women's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing departments for males stock trousers and shirts, not women's blouses, and troopers famously curse.
